The actual expression is a serious RSS reading, not a neutral transcript. It preserves many of the frozen prose’s disagreements, and its `PROSE-ESCAPE` notes are a legitimate way to carry content RSS lacks as a native relation. But it also changes modalities, drops substantive reasons, and sometimes overstates what RSS carries natively. I separate defects that belong to the selected language (RSS), to the translator/expression, and to the reader/probe provenance. The frozen language and conjecture stay frozen; the repairs below are only recorded.

## 1. Exact duplication, provenance, and “inert”

Source:

> “Duplicate delivery of the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry adds nothing; authority does not accumulate by repetition.”

Expression:

> “Exact duplicates are inert; near-duplicates are candidates for conflict.”

RSS language:

> “Exact duplication: two deliveries are exact duplicates if all record fields and provenance are equal.”
> “Near-duplication: two deliveries share booking and revision but differ in kind, quantity, or expiry.”

This is a specific gap. The source’s duplicate rule attaches to the record fields: same booking, revision, kind, quantity, expiry. RSS exact duplication also requires provenance equality. A distinguishing case: two deliveries from different replicas or delivery events carry identical booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry. The source says the second adds nothing. Under RSS, they are not exact duplicates because provenance differs, and they are not near-duplicates because kind, quantity, and expiry do not differ. They fall between the two RSS relations. The expression does not resolve this.

The expression also says “inert,” which is stronger than the source’s “adds nothing” / “convey no additional authority.” A single delivery is not inert; it is the duplicate that adds no authority. The expression itself admits this in its meta-commentary: “Exact duplicates are inert” translates or strengthens “duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority.” That admission is good, but the repair is not made.

Locus: selected language plus translator. RSS’s exact-duplication definition introduces provenance in a way the source’s duplicate rule does not require; the translator then compounds it with “inert.”

Proposed repair, not installed: add a record-field duplicate relation that ignores provenance, or make provenance-difference a reading/open question; replace “inert” with “adds no authority beyond its duplicate” or “mutually redundant.”

## 2. Conflict liveness versus story liveness

Source:

> “the snapshot’s job is not to compute one timeless answer but to decide which conflicts are still alive.”

Expression:

> “it asks which stories are live under a reading.”

RSS has both `Conflict` and `Liveness`. In RSS, liveness is a property of stories; conflict is a situation in which two or more stories for the same booking at the same greatest revision are not exact duplicates. The source’s object of liveness is the conflict, not the individual story. The expression shifts the subject from conflict to story. A distinguishing case: two tied active holds at the greatest revision are both live as stories; the source’s question is whether the conflict between them remains live. The expression’s wording can lose that relational target.

Locus: translator. RSS has the vocabulary to distinguish them.

Proposed repair, not installed: say “which conflicts remain live,” and define conflict liveness as a conflict whose constituent stories are live under the reading.

## 3. Lost modality and normativity

Several source claims are modal or normative; the expression renders them as flat assertions.

- Source: “A release or expired hold can reserve zero while an active hold reserves its quantity.”
  Expression: “An expired hold and a release reserve zero; an active hold reserves its quantity.”
  The source’s “can” is lost. RSS later treats expiry and release as reading-relative, so the flat assertion overcommits at that point.

- Source: “Different records tied at a greatest revision can remain unresolved alternatives.”
  Expression: “they remain unresolved alternatives.”
  Again, “can” becomes “remain.” The source permits retention of alternatives; the expression can sound as if it requires it.

- Source: “so the snapshot should retain the possibility that any one is the true one, or that none is…”
  Expression: “so the snapshot retains the possibility that any one is true, or that none is…”
  “Should retain” is normative; “retains” is descriptive.

Locus: translator. RSS can carry modality and normativity as account-level conjectures or readings.

Proposed repair, not installed: restore “can” and “should,” or qualify each as “under readings that do not merge/resolve.”

## 4. Weakened criticism: “manufactures authority”

Source:

> “That is convenient, but it manufactures authority.”

Expression:

> “RSS carries this as a projection; it may manufacture authority because the snapshot did not authorize the choice.”

The source makes a definite criticism. The expression softens it to “may manufacture.” That is a vanished certainty. A distinguishing reading: a reconciler that collapses ties by largest quantity does manufacture authority, on the source’s account, because the snapshot did not authorize the choice. The expression’s “may” turns a criticism into a possibility.

Locus: translator. RSS can carry the stronger criticism as an account-level criticism.

Proposed repair, not installed: preserve the definite form or explicitly mark why it is being weakened.

## 5. Set, interval, and projection

Source:

> “availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one.”

Expression:

> “availability is not a single number; RSS carries multiple possible reservations.”
> “RSS carries these as projections.”

RSS’s `Projection` is a function to a single answer. Lower and upper bounds are not one projection; they are two bounds. The source’s “set or interval” is a structured object that can lose correlations. The expression marks convexity as a `PROSE-ESCAPE`, which is good, but it does not preserve the set/interval distinction. A distinguishing case: the possible reservations for two bookings may form a non-convex set, and the interval bounds may include combinations that are not jointly realizable. The expression’s “multiple possible reservations” is too thin to carry that.

Locus: selected language plus translator. RSS lacks a native family/partial-order/interval primitive; the expression could have marked that lack more explicitly instead of saying “RSS carries these as projections.”

Proposed repair, not installed: add or mark a family-of-possible-reservations primitive, or explicitly say that lower/upper bounds are two projections and that the interval structure is carried only as prose/account conjecture.

## 6. Omitted substantive reasons and qualifications

The expression drops several source qualifications that RSS could carry as account-level prose or open questions. These are not cases where RSS proves impossibility; they are translator/reader omissions.

- Source: “That preserves honesty but makes downstream decisions harder.”
  Expression: omitted from the first disagreement.

- Source: “The second remains a live conjecture, especially if one thinks expired records are no longer ‘delivered records’ in the relevant sense.”
  Expression: “The second remains a live conjecture.” The rationale/condition is lost.

- Source: “Preserving that distinction matters because one can reject a rule while accepting the data, or accept the rule while rejecting the data as corrupt or late.”
  Expression: omitted. This is the substantive point of the criticism-target distinction.

- Source: “if two records share booking and revision but differ in kind or quantity, are they duplicates or alternatives?”
  Expression: “near-duplicates may be unresolved alternatives.” The explicit question is lost.

- Source: “That is a source assumption about what ‘release’ means.”
  Expression: omitted. This is a dependency between the release rule and a source assumption.

- Source: “where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently.”
  Expression: omitted from the criticism about pushing the problem downstream.

- Source: “because a negative number alone does not tell you which booking to revisit.”
  Expression: omitted from the conjecture about the sign of availability.

- Source: “That may be acceptable if the snapshot’s role is to support inquiry rather than to issue verdicts.”
  Expression: omitted from the eighth disagreement.

Locus: translator/reader. RSS’s account/inquiry structure can carry these as conjectures, criticisms, assumptions, or open questions.

Proposed repair, not installed: reinsert them as ordinary-prose account elements or open questions, without forcing them into native RSS relations.

## 7. “Described as replicated” becomes “is replicated”

Source:

> “The snapshot is described as replicated, but the bag is unordered.”

Expression:

> “The snapshot is replicated, but the bag is unordered.”

This is an introduced commitment. The source is reporting a description; the expression asserts the fact. A distinguishing reading: the snapshot might be described as replicated even if the bag is one replica’s view, a merge, or an incomplete union. The expression’s phrasing narrows that uncertainty.

Locus: translator.

Proposed repair, not installed: restore “described as” or mark the replication status as an assumption/open question.

## 8. Criticism targets: record/story conflation and overclaimed RSS elements

Source:

> “One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking’s history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful.”

Expression:

> “RSS carries criticism targets as elements: reading/rule, record/story, booking history, viewpoint/snapshot, coordinate/assumption.”

RSS’s primitives include `Reading`, `Story`, `Viewpoint`, `Coordinate`, and `Conflict`; it does not obviously have `Record` or `booking history` as native elements in the same way. More importantly, the slash “record/story” conflates two targets the source keeps separate. A criticism of a record with an implausible quantity is not the same as a criticism of a story drawn from that record. The expression’s own later discussion says a criticism of a rule is not the same as a criticism of a record, so the conflation is avoidable.

Locus: translator/language. RSS can carry some targets natively and others as account-level prose.

Proposed repair, not installed: distinguish `Record` and `Story` as criticism targets; say which are native RSS elements and which are carried as account-level prose.

## 9. Expiry: erase, demote, or change effect

Source:

> “But does expiry erase the record, demote it, or merely change its effect?”

Expression:

> “Under one reading, revision 5 expired and revision 3 active… Under another reading, expiry deletes the record from the bag…”

The expression covers deletion and effect-change, but drops demotion. A distinguishing case: expiry might leave the record present and superseding, but demote its authority or mark it inactive without deleting it. That is neither the first reading (high revision wins and reserves zero) nor the second (expiry deletes and lower revision becomes greatest). RSS can represent demotion as another reading.

Locus: translator.

Proposed repair, not installed: add demotion as a third reading.

## 10. Reader/probe provenance defects

The expression says:

> “without the withheld corpus field those attributions cannot be checked.”

But the frozen packet contains `corpus.text`. The corpus is not withheld in the frozen packet. This is a false provenance claim. It may be a probe artifact if the translator was run with a different visibility condition, but as frozen, the expression’s self-description is wrong. It can block checking of source attributions.

The expression also says:

> “The explicitly marked source quotations are the five `PROSE-ESCAPE` fragments.”

But the expression also quotes other source phrases without marking them as `PROSE-ESCAPE`, for example “this snapshot is inconsistent,” “higher revision always supersedes,” and “how much is available?”. This inventory is incomplete. It can confuse quotation with paraphrase or with RSS assertion.

Locus: reader/probe and translator/expression. These are not defects in RSS.

Proposed repair, not installed: check attributions against the actual `corpus_id` and `corpus.text`; mark all source quotations or explicitly distinguish quotation from paraphrase.

## 11. Language-level blocked criticisms

Some source criticisms are blocked or strained at the level of RSS itself, and the expression partly acknowledges this.

- Possibility smuggling: Source: “once you move to a set of possible worlds, you have smuggled in a notion of possibility that the original bag did not contain.” RSS supplies possibility vocabulary—accounts, readings, conjectures, open questions. The expression admits the circularity: RSS can register the criticism, but cannot make it fully in RSS vocabulary without already using the vocabulary the criticism targets. This is a genuine language-level tension, not a translator error. A proposed repair, not installed, would be a meta-level primitive or an explicit allowance for an account to criticize its own vocabulary in ordinary prose.

- Word-level criticism: Source: “the word ‘actually’ hides the problem.” RSS has no word-level or discourse-level relation. The expression marks this as `PROSE-ESCAPE`. That is a legitimate way to preserve the substantive prose objection, but it means the criticism is not carried by RSS relations.

- Hard/soft capacity: Source: “if availability is allowed to be negative, then capacity is not a hard constraint, and the word ‘capacity’ may be misleading; it is more like a soft target or a reporting threshold.” RSS has no native hard/soft constraint relation. The expression marks it as `PROSE-ESCAPE`. RSS could carry it as an account-level conjecture, but the expression does not do so except as escaped prose.

- Convexity and partial order: The source’s “possibly not even a convex one” and “a partial order of possible reservations, not a set” are marked as `PROSE-ESCAPE`. RSS lacks native relations for these. Again, this does not prove impossibility; an account could carry them as unanalyzed predicates or open conjectures. The expression’s choice to mark them as escapes is acceptable but not the only possible disposition.

## 12. What the expression preserves well

The expression correctly identifies the ten disagreements, preserves many source criticisms, and explicitly marks five `PROSE-ESCAPE` fragments. It admits its own circularity about possibility vocabulary, notes RSS’s lack of hard/soft constraint, convexity, partial order, and word-level criticism, and does not claim that RSS proves the source true. It also preserves the source’s final meta-point that false or incomplete proposals remain material for inquiry.

## Unresolved and competing interpretations

It remains unresolved whether RSS’s exact-duplication relation should include provenance or only record fields; whether “exact duplicates are inert” is a repair or a defect; whether the set/interval structure can be carried adequately by account-level prose; whether the source’s “conflicts remain live” is descriptive or normative; and whether the expression’s omissions are material losses or acceptable compression. These are legitimate competing readings.

The most supported diagnosis is mixed: some defects are in RSS itself—especially the provenance-laden exact-duplication definition and the lack of native set/interval/possibility relations—but many are in the translator’s expression: lost modality, weakened criticism, omitted reasons, overclaimed native RSS elements, and an incorrect “withheld corpus” provenance claim. A substantive prose objection remains admissible even where RSS cannot encode it, and the expression’s `PROSE-ESCAPE` notes are the right place to preserve those. The repairs above are recorded only; they are not installed in the frozen language or conjecture.

answer.body:
**RSS expression of the frozen warehouse prose**

In RSS, the frozen prose is carried as an inquiry state. Its subject is a viewpoint: a coordinate — capacity and logical current time — together with a bag of deliveries. Each delivery is evidence for a story about a booking. Exact duplicates are inert; near-duplicates are candidates for conflict. The snapshot is not a single ledger but a collection of rival stories.

The first conjecture in the source is that the snapshot’s job is not to compute one timeless answer but to decide which conflicts remain live. RSS carries this as: the account does not select a single projection by default; it asks which stories are live under a reading. Exact duplication adds no authority. Supersession is within a booking: a higher revision supersedes lower revisions for that booking, not across bookings. Different bookings can disagree without infecting each other.

For one booking, a reading groups stories by revision and keeps only the greatest revision present. At that greatest revision, a hold and a release are alternatives, not both in force. An expired hold and a release reserve zero; an active hold reserves its quantity. If several active holds tie at the greatest revision, they remain unresolved alternatives, not a sum and not a vote. RSS represents this as a conflict; it does not choose a reading that merges them. The source’s reason is a deliberate refusal: the rules do not say how to merge them, so the snapshot retains the possibility that any one is true, or that none is, depending on what “true” is taken to mean.

Availability is capacity minus whatever reservation is selected. The source adds a word-level criticism here: PROSE-ESCAPE “the word ‘actually’ hides the problem.” RSS has no word-level relation for what a word hides. Availability may still be negative if selected holds exceed capacity. Negative availability is a signal of over-promising relative to that reconstruction, not an arithmetic error. If bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a single number; RSS carries multiple possible reservations. The source’s further qualification is obstructed: PROSE-ESCAPE “possibly not even a convex one.” RSS has no convexity relation. A pessimistic reading takes the maximum hold among alternatives for each booking; an optimistic reading takes the minimum. Neither is forced by the snapshot.

Now the disagreements.

First disagreement: whether uncertainty should be retained. One account may collapse each tie to the largest quantity, earliest expiry, or a lexical tiebreak, producing a single availability number. RSS carries this as a projection; it may manufacture authority because the snapshot did not authorize the choice. Another account may keep all alternatives and report a range. The source says the snapshot does not settle which is correct; it only says tied records can remain unresolved. A conjecture in the source is: PROSE-ESCAPE “a partial order of possible reservations, not a set” is more useful because some alternatives may be compatible across bookings while others are not. It preserves many of the frozen prose’s disagreements, and its `PROSE-ESCAPE` notes are a legitimate way to carry content RSS lacks as a native relation. But it also changes modalities, drops substantive reasons, and sometimes overstates what RSS carries natively. I separate defects that belong to the selected language (RSS), to the translator/expression, and to the reader/probe provenance. The frozen language and conjecture stay frozen; the repairs below are only recorded.

## 1. Exact duplication, provenance, and “inert”

Source:

> “Duplicate delivery of the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry adds nothing; authority does not accumulate by repetition.”

Expression:

> “Exact duplicates are inert; near-duplicates are candidates for conflict.”

RSS language:

> “Exact duplication: two deliveries are exact duplicates if all record fields and provenance are equal.”
> “Near-duplication: two deliveries share booking and revision but differ in kind, quantity, or expiry.”

This is a specific gap. The source’s duplicate rule attaches to the record fields: same booking, revision, kind, quantity, expiry. RSS exact duplication also requires provenance equality. A distinguishing case: two deliveries from different replicas or delivery events carry identical booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry. The source says the second adds nothing. Under RSS, they are not exact duplicates because provenance differs, and they are not near-duplicates because kind, quantity, and expiry do not differ. They fall between the two RSS relations. The expression does not resolve this.

The expression also says “inert,” which is stronger than the source’s “adds nothing” / “convey no additional authority.” A single delivery is not inert; it is the duplicate that adds no authority. The expression itself admits this in its meta-commentary: “Exact duplicates are inert” translates or strengthens “duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority.” That admission is good, but the repair is not made.

Locus: selected language plus translator. RSS’s exact-duplication definition introduces provenance in a way the source’s duplicate rule does not require; the translator then compounds it with “inert.”

Proposed repair, not installed: add a record-field duplicate relation that ignores provenance, or make provenance-difference a reading/open question; replace “inert” with “adds no authority beyond its duplicate” or “mutually redundant.”

## 2. Conflict liveness versus story liveness

Source:

> “the snapshot’s job is not to compute one timeless answer but to decide which conflicts are still alive.”

Expression:

> “it asks which stories are live under a reading.”

RSS has both `Conflict` and `Liveness`. In RSS, liveness is a property of stories; conflict is a situation in which two or more stories for the same booking at the same greatest revision are not exact duplicates. The source’s object of liveness is the conflict, not the individual story. The expression shifts the subject from conflict to story. A distinguishing case: two tied active holds at the greatest revision are both live as stories; the source’s question is whether the conflict between them remains live. The expression’s wording can lose that relational target.

Locus: translator. RSS has the vocabulary to distinguish them.

Proposed repair, not installed: say “which conflicts remain live,” and define conflict liveness as a conflict whose constituent stories are live under the reading.

## 3. Lost modality and normativity

Several source claims are modal or normative; the expression renders them as flat assertions.

- Source: “A release or expired hold can reserve zero while an active hold reserves its quantity.”
  Expression: “An expired hold and a release reserve zero; an active hold reserves its quantity.”
  The source’s “can” is lost. RSS later treats expiry and release as reading-relative, so the flat assertion overcommits at that point.

- Source: “Different records tied at a greatest revision can remain unresolved alternatives.”
  Expression: “they remain unresolved alternatives.”
  Again, “can” becomes “remain.” The source permits retention of alternatives; the expression can sound as if it requires it.

- Source: “so the snapshot should retain the possibility that any one is the true one, or that none is…”
  Expression: “so the snapshot retains the possibility that any one is true, or that none is…”
  “Should retain” is normative; “retains” is descriptive.

Locus: translator. RSS can carry modality and normativity as account-level conjectures or readings.

Proposed repair, not installed: restore “can” and “should,” or qualify each as “under readings that do not merge/resolve.”

Source:

> “That is convenient, but it manufactures authority.”

Expression:

> “RSS carries this as a projection; it may manufacture authority because the snapshot did not authorize the choice.”

A distinguishing reading: a reconciler that collapses ties by largest quantity does manufacture authority, on the source’s account, because the snapshot did not authorize the choice. The expression’s “may” turns a criticism into a possibility.

Locus: translator. RSS can carry the stronger criticism as an account-level criticism.

## 5. Set, interval, and projection

Source:

> “availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one.”

> “availability is not a single number; RSS carries multiple possible reservations.”
